To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of intensive chemotherapy and anticancer vaccines in the treatment of patients with aggressive hematologic malignancy is feasible, safe and induces a high level of cancer-specific T cell immunity.

the combination of intensive chemotherapy and vaccination therapy can induce long lasting cancer-specific immune responses and that this strategy should be further evaluated as a treatment for patients with aggressive cancers.
the combination of intensive chemotherapy and stem cell transplants with anticancer vaccines can be used to treat aggressive hematological malignancy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of cancer patients.
the development of new treatment strategies for patients with cancer.
the development of a combined cancer treatment regimen that includes conventional chemotherapy, autologous stem transplantation and vaccination therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vaccination therapy is a promising therapeutic approach in the treatment of cancer but the results of the initial studies have to be confirmed in prospective randomised clinical trials.
the use of anticancer vaccines in the treatment of human malignancies should probably be integrated in the overall treatment regimen and not used as a single modality.
vaccination strategies should be combined with optimalization of immunoregulation and that this should be combined with intensive chemotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intensive chemotherapy and anticancer vaccination are complementary treatment modalities that should be combined in order to achieve maximal anticancer effect.
intensive cancer therapy is a safe procedure and that it may be combined with vaccination therapy to improve the outcome of the treatment.
the combination of conventional chemotherapy and vaccination therapy is a feasible and safe strategy for cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of intensive chemotherapies and anticancer vaccines can induce durable antitumor immunity and clinical responses in some cancer patients.
vaccination therapy can be used in patients with advanced disease, even after intensive chemotherapy and stem cell transplants.

the combination of intensive chemotherapy and anticancer vaccination therapy is feasible, and the results of our clinical trials indicate that such combinatory regimens are safe, and they may be effective.
